name: Koryak
confidence_why: The second-syllable coding rests on Gordon 2002 and StressTyp2 (Goedemans, Heinz & van der Hulst 2015) citing Zhukova 1972, whose provisional stress paragraph does not say it, and the one first-hand description, Kurebito 2004, instead gives initial stress in disyllables and second-syllable stress in longer words, skipping schwa and avoiding the final syllable.

audit.recode_to: Re-enter (or at minimum re-reason) on Kurebito 2004:141-142 + Zhukova 1972:40-41: disyllables initial; longer words stress the 2nd syllable and every second syllable thereafter, never the final — beat strings stress placement coded per word length as 10 010 0100 01010 010100 0101010 01010100 (1 = a stressed syllable) — with fences: (a) schwa-sensitive shifts (initial ə -> 01 in disyllables; 2nd-syllable ə -> retraction to 1st), (b) neither source ranks primary vs secondary (Kurebito marks all beats alike; Zhukova 'весьма условно'), (c) Kurebito's data are mainland (Severo-Evensk) Chawchuvan. If the catalog's scope test requires a unique PRIMARY at every length, keep OUT but change the reason from 'sources-undetermined' to 'rhythmic peninitial-nonfinal, primary undesignated, vowel-quality-sensitive (Kurebito 2004:142)'. Either way the StressTyp2 string second stress stays refuted at n=2 (both sources: initial) and at n>=5 (iterative beats, not a single peninitial).
audit.reasoning: Quote check: the record carries no quotation, but the deciding pages (Zhukova 1972 §41, pp.40-41) are held as a full scan plus 300-dpi page scan and every phrase the compilers note relies on is verbatim there; the StressTyp2-contradiction note is also correct (no peninitial statement on those pages; Gordon 2002:494 cites Zhukova 1972 for it). Deciding source: the standard 1972 reference grammar, whose stress paragraph is explicitly provisional. Best available: NO before today — Kurebito 2004 'A Report on Koryak Phonology' (ELPR A2-043, open access at TUFS) was unknown to the record and to the 2026-08-18 lit review; downloaded, scanned (no text, 250 dpi, sequential tesseract) and read from page scan. Its §4.3 states a determinate rule: disyllables initial; >2 syllables 'stress falls on every second syllable, starting from the second syllable, excluding the final syllable', with schwa-conditione

tone.quote: § 41. Ударение — многоаспектное явление, не изученное в корякском языке. [...] В корякском языке ударение не используется для образования слов или форм словоизменения. [...] Для корякского и всей группы чукотско-камчатских языков остается неизученным весь комплекс просодических элементов. Некоторые факты нашли морфологическую интерпретацию. [...] Описание интонации выходит за рамки описания фонологии слова. Изучению системы просодических средств в языках чукотско-камчатской группы едва положено начало.
tone.locator: §41 'Об ударении', pp. 40 (first two sentences) and 41 (last three)
tone.translation: §41. Stress is a many-sided phenomenon that has not been studied in Koryak. [...] In Koryak, stress is not used to form words or inflectional forms. [...] For Koryak and the whole group of Chukotko-Kamchatkan languages the entire complex of prosodic elements remains unstudied. Some facts have received a morphological interpretation. [...] A description of intonation lies beyond the description of word phonology. The study of the system of prosodic means in the Chukotko-Kamchatkan languages has barely begun.
tone.n_tones: None described: accent = stress only; prosodic system declared unstudied; no to…
tone.says: The grammar's only prosody section (§41) treats word accent purely as stress (ударение): hard to locate by ear in reduplicated disyllables, mostly initial in other disyllables, a tendency to the penult, alternating stressed/unstressed syllables in long words, main vs secondary stress 'provisional'; stress 'is not used to form words or inflectional forms'. Tone/pitch is never mentioned; the author states that 'the whole complex of prosodic elements remains unstudied' for Koryak and all Chukotko-…
